destination.name: Czech Republic
destination.pitch: Prague is three nights of beer halls and Gothic, and then the country gets better the further you go: one night in Český Krumlov, one in Brno for Tugendhat and the bone church, two in Mikulov for the Pálava hills and the wine cellars, and a

because.nature: Sandstone arches and gorge boats in Bohemian Switzerland, the limestone Pálava ridge above the Mikulov vineyards, the Vltava paddled through Krumlov; all of it gentle, none of it wild.
because.exploration: Cheap fast buses and trains, five bases inside three hours of each other, and towns that still close at ten and feel like themselves.
because.food: Tank Pilsner poured three ways in Prague's beer halls, roast pork and dumplings done properly at Lokál and Kuchyň, Ambiente's bakeries in Karlín, and Moravian Riesling and Pálava tasted in the cellar it was made in.
because.relaxation: Karlovy Vary's colonnades and thermal pool, Mikulov's slow wine afternoons and beer gardens in Prague that last until dark.
because.culture: Prague Castle, the Strahov library, Mucha, Schiele's Krumlov, Mies van der Rohe's Villa Tugendhat, two ossuaries and a Baroque theatre still run by candle-shaped bulbs.
because.adventure: A raft down the Vltava, a boat through the Kamenice gorges and a rope-railed sandstone path to Pravčická brána; that is the ceiling.
because.city: Prague is a proper capital with real nightlife and Brno is a student city with better bars than most capitals.

destination.caveat: Prague's centre is one of the most crowded square kilometres in Europe from May to September and the tourist-trap density on the Royal Way is real; the good food and the calm are in Karlín, Vinohrady and outside the capital, which means moving every night or two. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

cities.name: Prague
cities.base: Vinohrady or Karlín: ten minutes by tram or metro to the Old Town, the beer gardens and Ambiente's bakeries are on your street, and you sleep away from the stag parties. Three nights covers the castle

cities.name: Český Krumlov
cities.base: Inside the river loop or on Latrán under the castle. The town belongs to day-trippers from ten to five, so the point of sleeping here is the evening and the early morning when it is yours. One night i

cities.name: Brno
cities.base: Around Jakubské náměstí and Veveří, north of the main square: the standing pub, the cocktail bars and the tram to Tugendhat are all within ten minutes. One night if you have a Tugendhat booking, two i

cities.name: Mikulov
cities.base: Around Náměstí and Kostelní náměstí, under the castle; the wine bars close late and the walk up Svatý kopeček starts from the square. Two nights: one for the Pálava ridge and Pavlov, one for Valtice a

cities.name: Karlovy Vary
cities.base: The spa zone along the Teplá between the Mill Colonnade and the Pupp, where the springs, the funicular and the forest paths start at the door; the commercial town by the bus station is cheaper and dul

cities.name: Kutná Hora
cities.base: Not a base: an hour by train from Prague hlavní nádraží, ossuary at the Sedlec end and St Barbara's at the far end of town, back by late afternoon.

cities.name: Bohemian Switzerland (Hřensko)
cities.base: Not a base: the trailhead village for Pravčická brána and the Kamenice gorges, reached from Prague by train to Děčín and bus 434 or 438, or two hours by car. A whole day from Prague and worth it in Ap

outings.name: Pravčická brána and the Kamenice gorges
outings.why: The largest sandstone arch in Europe reached by the red trail from Tři prameny, then the Edmund and Wild gorges by punt; the hard part is transport, train to Děčín then bus 434 or 438, and the gorge boats run April to October only, so out o
outings.season: April to October for the boats; the arch is open daily late
outings.fallback: Pravčická brána alone from Tři prameny, 2 hours up and down, then the bus back.

outings.name: Kutná Hora: Sedlec ossuary and St Barbara's
outings.why: An hour by train to the silver town, the bone chapel first because it is timed-entry and by the station, then the 3 km walk through town to the cathedral; easy, but the ossuary needs a booked slot and forbids photographs.
outings.fallback: Ossuary and the Sedlec cathedral only, 3 hours door to door.

outings.name: The Vltava paddle through Krumlov
outings.why: A canoe or raft from Pískárna down to town, three or four hours of slow river, a couple of weirs to shoot and the castle above you at the end; you will get wet at the weirs and the river is busy on summer weekends.
outings.fallback: The one-hour town loop raft, 440 CZK, no weirs to speak of.

outings.name: Kleť on foot from Krumlov
outings.why: The 1,084 m hill above town with the oldest stone lookout tower in Bohemia and an Alps view on a clear day; a steady forest climb of about 600 m on the blue and red trails, nothing technical, but the chairlift from Krasetín runs weekends an
outings.season: All year; snow on top December to March
outings.fallback: The castle garden and the Křížová hora chapel loop above town, 2 hours.

outings.name: Punkva caves and the Macocha abyss
outings.why: Train to Blansko, bus to Skalní mlýn, then the guided walk and underground boat through the Punkva river cave to the bottom of the 138 m Macocha sinkhole; book the slot online days ahead in summer or you stand in a queue for nothing.
outings.season: All year; reduced tours and closed Mondays in winter
outings.fallback: Špilberk casemates and the ossuary in town, 3 hours.

outings.name: The Pálava ridge: Pavlov to Klentnice and Děvičky
outings.why: Bus or taxi to Pavlov, the Archeopark, then the red trail over the limestone ridge past Děvičky castle ruin, Děvín, Sirotčí hrádek and down into Mikulov with Café Fara in Klentnice for lunch; exposed and hot in July, and the Děvín summit is
outings.season: All year; the Archeopark is closed December to March
outings.fallback: Svatý kopeček above Mikulov and the Kozí hrádek tower, 2 hours.

outings.name: Valtice and Lednice
outings.why: The Salon vín in the Valtice chateau cellar in the morning, then bus or the 7 km cycle path to Lednice for the chateau, the minaret and the park; the tasting is two hours and you drink it, so put Lednice second and take the bus back.
outings.season: Salon vín closed Mondays and all of January; Lednice tours d
outings.fallback: Valtice only: the Salon vín and the chateau, back to Mikulov by 3 pm.

outings.name: Loket and the Ohře path
outings.why: Bus to the granite-rock town of Loket, a walk round the castle, then the 17 km riverside trail back along the Ohře through Svatošské skály to the edge of Karlovy Vary; flat and pretty and empty on weekdays, and you can bail at Doubí for a b
outings.fallback: The Diana funicular and the forest paths to Jelení skok, 2 hours.

places.name: Prague Castle and St Vitus Cathedral
places.note: Be at the Matthias Gate when the buildings open at 9:00, cathedral first, then the Old Royal Palace and Golden Lane; the 450 CZK circuit ticket covers all four, the grounds are free from 6:00, and winter hours close at 16:00.

places.name: Charles Bridge at dawn
places.note: Before 7:00 it is you, the statues and a few photographers; by 10:00 it is a slow-moving queue with caricaturists, so cross it early or late and never at midday.

places.name: Old Town Square and the Astronomical Clock
places.note: Walk through it because you will anyway, but the hourly clock show is forty seconds of wooden apostles watched by a thousand phones, and every restaurant on the square charges triple; do not eat or wait here.

places.name: Jewish Museum and the Old Jewish Cemetery
places.note: One Jewish Town ticket covers the Pinkas Synagogue with its 80,000 painted names, the layered cemetery and the Spanish Synagogue; closed Saturdays and Jewish holidays, summer closing is 18:00 and winter 16:30, and the Old-New Synagogue is a separate ticket.

places.name: Letná beer garden
places.note: Plastic cups of Gambrinus at picnic tables on the bluff above the bridges, the best cheap view in the city; it runs roughly April to October depending on weather and there is no table service, so queue at the kiosk.

places.name: Náplavka farmers' market
places.note: Saturday only, February to December: smoked fish, grilled sausages, cider and coffee on the embankment, then a beer from a boat-bar; go before 11:00 or it is shoulder to shoulder.

places.name: Lokál Dlouhááá
places.note: The Ambiente beer hall that made tank Pilsner and a proper svíčková respectable again; long tables, fried cheese, pork schnitzel, beers poured hladinka or šnyt on request, Sunday closes at 22:00 and it is busy enough to book.

places.name: U Zlatého tygra
places.note: Hrabal's pub, Pilsner only, no food to speak of, regulars own the tables and the waiter puts a beer down as you sit; arrive at 15:00 on the dot or you will not get in, and do not ask for a menu.

places.name: Kantýna
places.note: A butcher's shop in a former bank where you point at the cut, they weigh it and grill it, and you stand or grab a stool; tartare and the beef rib are the orders, no reservations, and the Sunday close is 22:00.

places.name: Eska
places.note: Bakery and restaurant in a converted Karlín factory: sourdough, potatoes in ash with smoked fish, and the best breakfast in the city; it opens at 09:00 on weekends and closes at 18:00 every day, so it is a morning or lunch place, not dinner.

places.name: Kuchyň
places.note: Ambiente's Czech kitchen in the Salm Palace on the castle square: you walk into the kitchen, lift the lids on the pots and choose, then eat on the terrace over the city; the sensible lunch after the castle instead of the Golden Lane tourist cafés.

places.name: Vinohradský pivovar
places.note: The neighbourhood brewery on Korunní with unfiltered 11 and 12 degree lagers, goulash and a pork knee, full of people who live within four streets; no English needed and Sunday closes at 22:00.

places.name: Sedlec Ossuary
places.note: The bones of some 40,000 people arranged into a chandelier and the Schwarzenberg coat of arms; timed tickets, 220 CZK, booked online in advance, no photographs since 2020, and the hours drop to 17:00 in October and March and 16:00 November to February.

places.name: Cathedral of the Assumption, Sedlec
places.note: Santini's Baroque-Gothic rebuild of a Cistercian church five minutes from the ossuary and almost empty; the combined ticket with the ossuary and St Barbara's makes it nearly free, and it opens later than the ossuary.

places.name: St Barbara's Cathedral
places.note: The miners' cathedral with a flying-buttress crown and frescoes of men at work, 120 CZK; April to October it is 9:00 to 18:00, winter 10:00 to 16:00 or 17:00, and the terrace of Jesuit statues outside it is the best view over the town.

places.name: Dačický
places.note: A beer-hall restaurant in a burgher house on Rakova with several regional lagers on tap and roast duck done properly; the tables in the vaulted room fill with tour lunches from 12:30, so eat at 11:30 or after 14:00.

places.name: Pravčická brána
places.note: Europe's largest natural sandstone arch, reached by the red trail from the Tři prameny bus stop in about an hour of steady climbing; 125 CZK at the gate, daily late March to October and Friday to Sunday 10:00 to 16:00 in winter, and the Gabriela trail from Mezní Louka is still closed after the 2022

places.name: Edmundova soutěska boat
places.note: A punt poled through the narrowest stretch of the Kamenice between 50 m sandstone walls, guided, hourly departures of 20 to 25 people and no advance booking; reopened in 2026 after the fire closures, 350 CZK, June to October only, so check the season before building a day on it.

places.name: Divoká soutěska boat
places.note: The upstream gorge boat, 200 CZK, April to October 9:00 to 17:00, reached on foot from Mezná village or from Mezní Louka; quieter than Edmund's and the ferryman's jokes are the same, so if you do one, do this one.

places.name: Český Krumlov Castle, Route I
places.note: The guided route through the Rosenberg and Eggenberg rooms and the Masquerade Hall, closed Mondays and closed entirely November to March; book the English slot online, the 09:00 tour beats the coaches, and the summer close is 17:00.

places.name: Castle tower and museum
places.note: The painted round tower is the one thing at the castle open every day and self-guided; 162 steps, the whole loop of the river below you, and it stays open on Mondays and through the winter when the tours stop, closing 15:30 from November and closed Mondays then.

places.name: Baroque castle theatre
places.note: One of two 18th-century theatres in Europe with its original stage machinery, scenery and wind machines, shown on five short guided tours a day at 10:00, 11:00, 13:00, 14:00 and 15:00; May to October, closed Mondays, small groups, so book it with the castle ticket.

places.name: Castle garden and the Cloak Bridge
places.note: Free: out over the five-storey Cloak Bridge, through the courtyards to the terraced garden and the revolving auditorium; the garden is open May to October, 17:00 close in October, and at 19:00 on a summer evening it is nearly empty.

places.name: Egon Schiele Art Centrum
places.note: A former brewery on Široká with a room on Schiele's 1911 summer here, when the town ran him out for painting local girls, plus rotating modern shows; open daily, and the one indoor thing to do when the rain comes in.

places.name: Museum Fotoateliér Seidel
places.note: The Seidel family's Art Nouveau photo studio and house across the river, left as it was in the 1950s with the glass plates and the darkroom; almost no one crosses the bridge to it, and the caretaker will show you the studio camera.

places.name: Krčma v Šatlavské
places.note: The old jail turned into a cellar with an open fire and meat on spits; it is theatre and it knows it, but the pork and the sausages are done over real coals and it is fun at 21:00 when the day-trippers have gone, so book a table.

places.name: Laibon
places.note: Vegetarian in a vaulted room with a terrace right on the river below the castle: dhal, sabji, dumplings without the pork, and the best lunch table in town for the price; no reservations for the terrace, so come at 11:30.

places.name: Hospoda Na Louži
places.note: An old pub on Kájovská with wooden booths, Eggenberg beer and goulash with bread dumplings at prices that have not chased the tourists; it is small and family-run, so a wait at 19:00 is normal.

places.name: Papa's Living Restaurant
places.note: Riverside terrace under the castle with a mixed Czech and Italian menu, decent steaks and pasta; you pay for the view and the view is worth it at dusk, so book a terrace table.

places.name: Maleček rafting and canoe hire
places.note: Two-person canoes or rafts from about 770 CZK a head for the Pískárna to Krumlov run, 3 to 4 hours with a van to the start; May to September, book a day ahead in July and August, and the one-hour town loop at 440 CZK is the version for the nervous.

places.name: Seminární zahrada viewpoint
places.note: The small terrace garden behind the museum on Horní street with the postcard angle on the castle and tower across the river; free, two minutes from the square, best at sunset when the tower lights come on.

places.name: Villa Tugendhat
places.note: Mies van der Rohe's 1930 glass house with the onyx wall and the retracting windows, the reason architects come to Brno; closed Mondays, 450 CZK basic or 500 extended, and tickets go on sale two months ahead and sell out in days, so if you have no booking the garden and exhibition are free and the ex

places.name: Ossuary at St James
places.note: Found under the square in 2001, the second largest ossuary in Europe after Paris with the bones of 50,000 laid in lit, silent vaults with a soundtrack; 180 CZK, closed Mondays, twenty minutes and stranger than Sedlec because nobody is posing.

places.name: Labyrinth under the Vegetable Market
places.note: A kilometre of medieval cellars under the market with a wine vault, an alchemist's lab and a pillory; 200 CZK, last entry 17:30, closed Mondays, and English-guided tours only at 13:00 and 15:00 Saturday and 11:00 Sunday, otherwise self-guided.

places.name: Zelný trh market
places.note: The vegetable market has traded on the sloping square since the 13th century: Moravian apricots and strawberries in season, flowers, honey and a sausage stand, Monday to Saturday and gone by early afternoon; the Baroque Parnas fountain and the Reduta theatre frame it.

places.name: Špilberk castle and casemates
places.note: The Habsburg prison on the hill over the centre: the casemates where Italian and Czech political prisoners were held are 180 CZK and closed Mondays, the ramparts and park are free all day, and the walk up from Husova takes ten minutes.

places.name: 10-Z nuclear bunker
places.note: A Cold War shelter for the regional Party elite tunnelled into the Špilberk rock and left with its 1960s filters, bunks and telephones; self-guided or with a guide, closed Mondays, and you can sleep in it as a hostel if that is your thing.

places.name: Café Era
places.note: A 1929 functionalist café by Josef Kranz five minutes' walk from Villa Tugendhat, restored with its white curves and the spiral stair; the natural coffee stop before or after the villa, and a lunch place on weekdays.

places.name: Bistro Franz
places.note: A neighbourhood bistro on Veveří with a short seasonal menu from local farms, Moravian wines by the glass and a proper breakfast; closed Mondays, and the daily lunch menu is one of the best deals in the city.

places.name: Výčep Na stojáka
places.note: A standing-only taproom in the First Republic style with rotating small-brewery lagers, and on a warm night the whole square outside is the pub; weekends open at 14:00, and it is where Brno actually drinks.

places.name: Lokál U Caipla
places.note: The Brno outpost of Prague's Lokál in a long vaulted room: tank Pilsner, fried cheese, beef in cream sauce, and a cheap daily lunch; reliably good, reliably full, so book for dinner.

places.name: Bar, který neexistuje
places.note: The Bar That Doesn't Exist, a long wooden counter with a bottle wall and the bartenders who started Brno's cocktail scene; no menu needed, say what you like, and the sister bar Super Panda Circus around the corner is the weirder second stop.

places.name: Punkva caves and Macocha
places.note: Train to Blansko, bus to Skalní mlýn, then an hour underground on foot and by boat on the Punkva to the floor of the Macocha abyss; timed tickets sell out weeks ahead in summer, book on the caves' website, and closed Mondays November to March.

places.name: Mikulov castle
places.note: The Dietrichstein castle on the rock over the square holds the regional museum, a wine-making exhibition and a 1643 barrel that held 100,000 litres; 180 CZK, closed Mondays May to September, Friday to Sunday only in April, October and November, and shut in winter.

places.name: Svatý kopeček
places.note: The pilgrimage hill above town, a Way of the Cross up to the St Sebastian chapel and a bell tower, with the castle, the Pálava and Austria laid out below; forty minutes up from the square, and at sunset it is the best thing in Mikulov.

places.name: Jewish quarter and cemetery
places.note: Mikulov was the seat of Moravia's chief rabbi and half the town was Jewish in 1800; the Upper Synagogue on Husova is a small museum and the cemetery of 4,000 stones up the hill is one of the largest in the country, closed Saturdays, key from the ceremonial hall.

places.name: Vinotéka Volařík
places.note: The town wine bar of the Volařík family, Mikulov's best-known producer, with their Pálava, Welschriesling and Riesling by the glass at a table looking at the church and the castle; the easy first tasting, and the shop sells the bottle you liked.

places.name: Vinný sklep Pod Kozím hrádkem
places.note: A cellar cut into the limestone under the tower with guided tastings of eight to ten local wines by the cellarmaster; call or book ahead because it opens for groups and evenings rather than to a fixed timetable, and it is the cellar-in-the-rock experience Mikulov is about.

places.name: Prostě SKLEP
places.note: A working cellar with a summer terrace facing Svatý kopeček, run by a young winemaker pouring his own and neighbours' wines by the glass; hours shift with the season and the harvest, so check the day before, and it is a fifteen-minute walk from the square.

places.name: Sojka & spol.
places.note: A bistro and wine shop on the main square that does the local pairings right: Moravian sausages, goat cheese from the Pálava farms, a daily lunch menu and a long list of the region's small growers by the glass; the lunch stop between cellars.

places.name: Sonberk winery
places.note: A glass-and-timber winery on a slope over the Nové Mlýny lakes with the Pálava ridge across the water, open daily 10:00 to 18:00 and until 20:00 on summer Fridays and Saturdays; the Pálava grape and the late-harvest Rieslings are the point, it needs a taxi or a bike from Mikulov, and it closes for w

places.name: Salon vín, Valtice
places.note: The national wine competition's top 100 sit open in the Valtice chateau cellar and 725 CZK buys two hours with a glass and a spit bucket, the single best way to understand Moravian wine; closed Mondays and all January, Sundays only June to September, later closing Friday and Saturday, and bus 570 fr

places.name: Lednice chateau and park
places.note: The Liechtenstein neo-Gothic palace with a carved wooden staircase, an 1845 palm house and a park with a minaret and a boat to it; tours are closed Mondays and drop to weekends only from October, the park is free and open all day, and it pairs with Valtice on one bus day.

places.name: Archeopark Pavlov
places.note: A concrete museum sunk into the hill where the mammoth hunters camped 30,000 years ago, the Věstonice Venus's neighbours; 150 CZK, closed Mondays May to September, Friday to Sunday only in April, October and November, shut December to March, and the start of the ridge walk to Děvičky.

places.name: Café Fara, Klentnice
places.note: A former rectory under Sirotčí hrádek turned into the best lunch on the Pálava, with a garden, homemade lemonade, Moravian plates and cakes; it is the halfway point of the ridge walk, full on sunny weekends, and hours shorten in winter.

places.name: Mill Colonnade and the springs
places.note: Buy a porcelain spout cup for 150 CZK and walk the 1881 neo-Renaissance colonnade sipping from five springs between 30 and 65 degrees; they taste of iron and eggs and the locals drink them straight-faced, and the colonnade is free and open all hours.

places.name: Vřídlo, the Hot Spring
places.note: The 72-degree geyser throwing 2,000 litres a minute 12 m into the air inside its 1970s glass hall; free, loud, and the underground tour of the mineral-crusted pipes below it is a short paid extra worth doing.

places.name: Diana funicular and lookout tower
places.note: The 1912 funicular from behind the Grandhotel Pupp to a 35 m brick tower with the whole valley below and forest paths back down via Jelení skok; runs every fifteen minutes, 17:00 close in winter and 18:00 in April and October, and it was shut for track repairs for most of September 2026.

places.name: Becherovka visitor centre
places.note: The herbal liqueur's original 1867 factory turned into a tour of cellars and barrels ending in a tasting of the range; 290 CZK, hourly slots of ten people that must be pre-booked, closed Mondays and a lunch break from 12:00 to 12:30.

places.name: Moser glassworks and museum
places.note: The crystal works founded in 1857 with a museum of 2,000 pieces and a factory floor where you watch the glassblowers; the works tour runs weekdays 9:00 to 14:00 only and must be reserved, the museum is Monday to Saturday, and bus 1 or 22 gets you there.

places.name: Saunia Thermal pool
places.note: The outdoor pool on the roof of the Brutalist Hotel Thermal, 32 and 38 degree spring water and eight saunas with the town lit up below; open daily until 23:00, pay by the hour, and it is the cheapest way to do the spa thing without a doctor's note.

places.name: Charleston
places.note: The restaurant locals name first: beef cheeks, roast goose, mushroom soup and strudel in a 1930s room with a pianist some evenings; off the spa strip on Bulharská, weekends open at 11:00, and prices are half what the colonnade hotels charge.

places.name: Restaurace Promenáda
places.note: The old-school white-tablecloth place in the spa zone, venison, duck and a long Moravian wine list, where the film festival crowd eats in July; the one dinner worth the spa-zone prices, and book.

places.name: Sklípek
places.note: A tiny cellar pub near the market with six tables, Czech classics and a daily lunch menu under 200 CZK, full of office workers at noon; Sunday closed, no English menu, and the sort of place the spa zone no longer has.

places.name: Café Elefant
places.note: The 1870s coffee house on the promenade with cakes under glass and a terrace on the Teplá where Goethe's generation sat; the coffee is fine, the cake is the point, and a spa wafer from the stand outside is the cheaper alternative.

places.name: Grandhotel Pupp
places.note: The 1701 hotel that played the Casino Royale in the Bond film; walk through the lobby, then leave, because a coffee costs what a dinner does at Charleston and the terrace is for hotel guests.

places.name: Loket castle and town
places.note: A Gothic castle on a granite crag inside a loop of the Ohře, twenty minutes by bus, with a torture museum, a porcelain collection and a square that has not been spoiled; 16:30 close in winter, and the riverside path back to Karlovy Vary makes it a whole day.
